nodes.name: Kochen-Specker (KS) set
nodes.statement: A finite set of unit vectors $\mathcal{V}$ in $\mathcal{H}=\mathbb{C}^d$ ($d \ge 3$) admitting no assignment $f:\mathcal{V}\to\{0,1\}$ with $f(u)+f(v)\le 1$ for orthogonal $u,v$ and $\sum_{u\in b} f(u)=1$ for every orthonormal basis $b\subseteq\mathcal{V}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A finite set of unit vectors that cannot be consistently assigned 0/1 values respecting the noncontextual KS rules.

nodes.name: Yu-Oh set
nodes.statement: The state-independent contextuality set of 13 unit vectors in $\mathbb{C}^3$ that admits KS assignments only if at most one of its four nonwhite (central) nodes is assigned $1$.

nodes.name: Complete orthogonal basis (within a KS set)
nodes.statement: An orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{C}^d$ all of whose vectors belong to the KS set $\mathcal{V}$; e.g. $\{(0,0,1),(0,1,0),(1,0,0)\}$ is complete, while completing $\{\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(0,1,-1), \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(1,1,1)\}$ requires a vector outside $\mathcal{V}$.

nodes.name: State-independent contextuality (SI-C) set
nodes.statement: A set of vectors that exhibits state-independent contextuality. Every KS set is SI-C, but not every SI-C set is a KS set; the Yu-Oh set is the minimal SI-C set in any dimension.
nodes.origin_citation: Cabello, Kleinmann & Portillo 2016, J. Phys. A 49, 38LT01

nodes.name: Weyl-Heisenberg group generators in $d=3$
nodes.statement: The cyclic shift $X$ and the clock $Z$: $X = \begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $Z = \begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&\omega&0\\0&0&\omega^2\end{pmatrix}$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}$, satisfying the canonical commutation relations.
nodes.origin_citation: Weyl 1931, The Theory of Groups and Quantum Mechanics

nodes.name: SIC-POVM
nodes.statement: A symmetric, informationally complete, positive operator-valued measure: a set of $d^2$ rank-one projectors in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with pairwise equal inner products.

nodes.name: Majorana representation
nodes.statement: Every pure spin-$1$ state (unit vector in $\mathbb{C}^3$) is uniquely represented by two (possibly coinciding) points on the unit sphere, viewed as the directions of two symmetrized spin-$1/2$ constituents.

nodes.name: Three vertex types of the Cabello-33 KS set
nodes.statement: The 33 vertices partition into three orbits under graph automorphisms: (I) the $3$ vectors of Eq.~\eqref{type1}; (II) the $12$ non-type-I vertices in Eqs.~\eqref{type2a}--\eqref{type2b}; (III) the $18$ non-type-I vertices in Eqs.~\eqref{type3a}--\eqref{type3b}.

nodes.name: Alice's bases $x=1,\dots,4$ (type ii)
nodes.statement: Four bases of the form $\{(\pm 1,\pm\omega,\pm\omega^2),(\pm 1,\pm 1,\pm 1),(\pm\omega^2,\omega,\pm 1)\}$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}$ (signs as in Eqs.~\eqref{type2a}--\eqref{type2b}).

nodes.name: Bob's nine bases (type iii)
nodes.statement: Nine bases each containing one of $\{(0,0,1),(0,1,0),(1,0,0)\}$ together with two vectors of the form $(*,*,0)$, $(*,0,*)$ or $(0,*,*)$ with entries in $\{1,-1,\omega,-\omega\}$ (Eqs.~\eqref{type3a}--\eqref{type3b}).

nodes.name: Maximally entangled qutrit-qutrit state
nodes.statement: $|\psi\rangle = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\sum_{j=0}^{2} |j\rangle\otimes|j\rangle$

nodes.name: Weyl-Heisenberg generators $X$, $Z$
nodes.statement: $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix},\;\;Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&\omega&0\\0&0&\omega^2\end{pmatrix}$

nodes.name: Cabello-33 KS theorem (14-basis 33-vector KS set in $\mathbb{C}^3$)
nodes.statement: The 33 unit vectors of Fig.~1, organized into 14 complete orthogonal bases, form a Kochen-Specker set in dimension three.
assumptions: The 33 vectors include the Yu-Oh 13-vector set (upper triangle of Fig.~1)
The remaining 20 vectors form three additional mutually orthogonal triples (red, green, blue, yellow) plus the small triangles
conclusions: No assignment $f:\mathcal{V}\to\{0,1\}$ satisfies the KS conditions
The set has exactly $14$ complete orthogonal bases, the current minimum in $d=3$

nodes.name: Proof of KS impossibility for the Cabello-33 set
nodes.statement: Color-counting argument: the embedded Yu-Oh subset forces at most three $1$-assignments while the four mutually orthogonal color triples (red, green, blue, yellow) each require exactly one $1$.

nodes.name: Invoke Yu-Oh constraint
nodes.statement: The 13 vectors in the upper triangle of Fig.~1 are the Yu-Oh set, which admits KS assignments only if at most one of its four nonwhite nodes is assigned $1$.

nodes.name: Color triples force one $1$ each
nodes.statement: The three red (and likewise green, blue, yellow) nodes are mutually orthogonal, so any KS assignment must put exactly one $1$ in each color class.

nodes.name: Pigeonhole contradiction
nodes.statement: Only three $1$'s fit (one per Yu-Oh-compatible position) but four colors each demand a $1$, so no consistent KS assignment exists.

nodes.name: Bipartite nonlocal game with $|X|=5$, $|Y|=9$
nodes.statement: With probability $\pi(x,y)$, Alice receives a basis $x\in X$ ($|X|=5$) and Bob a basis $y\in Y$ ($|Y|=9$); each outputs one vector from their basis. They win iff their output vectors are not orthogonal.
assumptions: All $|X|\times|Y|=45$ context combinations are equally likely

nodes.name: Qutrit-qutrit perfect quantum strategy for the $5\times 9$ game
nodes.statement: Alice and Bob share $|\psi\rangle = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\sum_j |j\rangle\otimes|j\rangle$ and each measures their qutrit in the basis given by the referee, outputting the result; this guarantees nonorthogonal outputs.
output: Alice outputs the vector of basis $x$ corresponding to her measurement outcome
Bob outputs the vector of basis $y$ corresponding to his outcome
Outputs are guaranteed not orthogonal, achieving $W_Q=1$

nodes.name: Distribute bases to Alice and Bob
nodes.statement: Referee assigns Alice a basis from types (i)+(ii) (5 bases) and Bob a basis from type (iii) (9 bases) with probability $\pi(x,y)$.

nodes.name: Joint measurement of $|\psi\rangle$
nodes.statement: Each player projectively measures their half of $|\psi\rangle$ in the assigned basis and outputs the basis vector corresponding to their outcome.

nodes.name: Output nonorthogonal vectors
nodes.statement: Because $|\psi\rangle$ correlates outcomes via $\langle a|\otimes\langle b|\,|\psi\rangle \propto \langle a|b^*\rangle$, the produced output pair is never orthogonal, yielding $W_Q=1$.

nodes.name: Refutation of Cabello 2025 Conjecture 2
nodes.statement: Conjecture 2 of [Cabello, PRL 134, 010201 (2025)] (qutrit-qutrit perfect strategy with minimum $|X|\times|Y|$ has $|X|=7,\ |Y|=9$ via Peres-33/Penrose-33) is false: the new KS set yields a $5\times 9$ perfect strategy.
assumptions: The Cabello-33 KS set with 14 bases (TP469.1)
The bipartite game and quantum strategy of AP469.1
conclusions: There exists a qutrit-qutrit perfect quantum strategy with $|X|=5$ and $|Y|=9$

nodes.name: Minimality of $|X|\times|Y|$ within the new KS set
nodes.statement: Using the method of Trandafir-Cabello (2025), no other distribution of the 14 bases of this KS set yields a perfect quantum strategy with smaller $|X|\times|Y|$ than $5\times 9$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness up to unitaries
nodes.statement: The Cabello-33 KS set is unique up to unitary transformations, in contrast to Peres-33 and Penrose-33 which are not.
nodes.origin_citation: Trandafir & Cabello 2026 (in preparation); method of Xu et al. 2022, PRL 129, 050402

nodes.name: Weyl-Heisenberg construction of the KS set
nodes.statement: Acting with $X$ on the minimal SI-C (Yu-Oh) set keeps one within the SI-C set; acting twice with $Z$ on the SI-C set yields the Cabello-33 KS set.
assumptions: The starting set is the minimal SI-C set (Yu-Oh)
conclusions: The full 33-vector KS set is generated by the orbit of the Yu-Oh set under $\langle X,Z^2\rangle$

nodes.name: Two unitarily inequivalent SIC-POVMs inside the KS set
nodes.statement: Acting with both $X$ and $Z$ on $\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1,1,0)$ produces one SIC-POVM; doing so on $\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1,-1,0)$ produces a unitarily inequivalent SIC-POVM. Both lie inside the 33-vector KS set.

nodes.name: Yu-Oh subset conjecture for simplest qutrit KS set
nodes.statement: The simplest qutrit KS set must contain the Yu-Oh set (the minimal set exhibiting state-independent contextuality).

nodes.name: Cabello-33 reaches the natural lower limit
nodes.statement: The 14-basis 33-vector KS set introduced here is at the true natural limit for the smallest qutrit KS set; the author is actively working to prove this.

nodes.name: Independence-number bound for classical winning probability
nodes.statement: The maximal classical winning probability of a nonlocal game whose winning combinations form an orthogonality graph $G$ on $N$ vertices over $C$ contexts equals $\alpha(G)/C$, where $\alpha(G)$ is the independence number.
assumptions: Game's winning conditions are encoded in the orthogonality graph $G$

nodes.name: Explicit $5\times 9$ context game with $W_C=44/45$, $W_Q=1$
nodes.statement: Of the $45$ context combinations: $9$ share a common vector (5 winning vs.\ 4 losing output combinations each) and $36$ involve one orthogonal pair (8 winning vs.\ 1 losing each); summing gives $9\cdot 5 + 36\cdot 8 = 333$ winning combinations, yielding $W_C=44/45$ classically and $W_Q=1$ with the maximally entangled state.

nodes.name: Majorana representation of the 33 vectors
nodes.statement: Each of the 33 KS vectors is depicted as a unique pair of points on the unit sphere (Fig.~2); some Majorana points are shared across vectors. Examples: $(1,0,0)\to$ two points at the north pole; $(0,1,0)\to$ one point at each pole; $(0,0,1)\to$ two points at the south pole.

nodes.name: Bases as the true measure of physical simplicity
nodes.statement: The number of complete orthogonal bases—not the number of vectors—is the meaningful complexity measure: it sets the minimal sum of Alice's and Bob's inputs in the corresponding bipartite perfect strategy.

nodes.name: Alternative KS-set definitions
nodes.statement: Some authors adopt a stricter KS-set definition requiring additional vectors and bases (cf. Trandafir & Cabello 2025, arXiv:2503.02974).

nodes.name: Comparison table of small qutrit KS sets
nodes.statement: Table 1 compares Schutte-33, Conway-Kochen-31, Peres-33, Penrose-33, and the new set on (number of bases, vertex types, automorphism-group order, minimal bipartite perfect strategy): the new set achieves $14$ bases, $3$ vertex types, symmetry $144$, and $5$-$9$ perfect strategy.

nodes.name: Yu-Oh minimality for SI-C
nodes.statement: The Yu-Oh set is the minimal set of vectors (in any dimension) that allows for state-independent contextuality.
nodes.origin_citation: Cabello, Kleinmann & Portillo 2016, J. Phys. A 49, 38LT01

nodes.name: KS sets necessary for nonsignaling-limit bipartite correlations and pseudotelepathy
nodes.statement: KS sets are necessary for bipartite correlations attaining the nonsignaling limit, and (via Liu et al. 2024) for bipartite perfect strategies ("quantum pseudotelepathy") and bipartite correlations with maximal nonlocal fraction.
nodes.origin_citation: Cabello 2025, PRL 134, 010201; Liu et al. 2024, PRR 6, L042035
